target_2_daily_journal_calendar_event_ch.ROOT_CAUSE: ClickCompletionToken is #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] (mcp/action.rs:177). The chip value must therefore be EITHER a parseable completion declaration OR the domain json the test reads off it - never both. The MT-117 merge fix adds calendar_event_id and daily_note_doc_id alongside the declaration keys, which makes parse_click_completion_token FAIL, so the driver sees NO declaration on the target and falls through to the generic disappeared path.
target_2_daily_journal_calendar_event_ch.the_conflict_stated_plainly: test_calendar_interop asserts argus_node_json_value_field_equals(tree, chip, "calendar_event_id", ...) - it requires the domain field at the TOP LEVEL of the chip value. The driver requires that same value to parse as a closed token. These are mutually exclusive. The chip carried NO declaration before MT-117, which is why the test passed at 31/0 then.
target_2_daily_journal_calendar_event_ch.why_the_mt042_shape_does_not_resolve_it_: MT-042 hit the identical collision and moved its STATE to a sibling {author_id}.state node so the declaration could own the value. That works when the sibling is what readers consult. Here the reader is a test this MT may not edit, and it reads the chip node itself.
target_2_daily_journal_calendar_event_ch.resolution_requires_an_authority_decisio: Three options, each touching a durable contract: (a) move the chip domain fields into the declaration semantic_value and update test_calendar_interop to read them there - forbidden to this MT, the test may not be edited; (b) relax ClickCompletionToken from deny_unknown_fields so a token may carry domain siblings - a product-wide schema change affecting every observer; (c) accept that this target cannot carry a declaration and exclude it from the PT-117-1 count with a typed reason. Not decided unilaterally.
